related_questions.question: Do you need vaccines to go to the Philippines?

text_blocks.snippet: While vaccination is not mandatory for entry into the Philippines, it is strongly recommended to ensure your routine vaccinations are up-to-date. Specifically, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends that travelers be current on vaccines for hepatitis A, hepatitis B, rabies, and typhoid, especially if visiting rural areas or engaging in outdoor activities. A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required only if arriving from a yellow fever-endemic country.
snippet_highlighted_words: vaccination is not mandatory for entry into the Philippines

list.snippet: Hepatitis A: Highly recommended due to potential exposure through contaminated food and water.
Hepatitis B: Recommended for travelers, particularly those at risk of exposure through medical procedures or sexual contact.
Typhoid: Recommended for travelers to smaller towns and rural areas.
Rabies: Recommended for travelers engaging in outdoor activities or visiting rural areas.
Japanese Encephalitis: Consider vaccination if visiting rural areas, especially during the wet season.
Malaria: Risk is variable, but antimalarials may be recommended for travel to certain islands or rural areas.

list.title: Yellow Fever:
list.snippet: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required for travelers arriving from countries with risk of yellow fever transmission.

list.title: Routine Vaccinations:
list.snippet: Ensure your routine vaccinations (e.g., measles, mumps, rubella, tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis) are up-to-date.

list.title: Travel Health Advice:
